components.gap: The construction or argument owed under the declared status proved=annex:p15.stieltjes-construction is not written out in full. The proof shows only that the infimum of F is its limit at minus infinity. It dismisses the upper end with 'The upper-end proof is the reversed argument' (annex line 296), which is a 'similarly' in place of written steps. That upper-end fact is needed later: F(infinity), defined as sup F, must be the limit of F at plus infinity, including when the supremum is infinite. The truncation argument for targets with right endpoint infinity relies on it ('Their upper F values increase to F(b) ... by the endpoint-limit argument', annex lines 383-385). Second, the stated conclusion 'Its values on bounded intervals are finite' (body lines 211-212) is never proved for bounded intervals other than the finite-endpoint members I(a,b). The monotonicity step from containment in some (-n,n] is not written. Annex lines 401-411 treat only the cover (-n,n] and sigma-finiteness.

The construction or argument owed under the declared status proved=annex:p15.cdf-existence depends on an unstated assumption, so a failure condition holds. The theorem concludes that the law of Q_F equals mu_F and is the unique Borel probability law with cumulative function F (body lines 297-299). For this the proof (annex lines 512-516) cites Theorem thm:p15-cdf-laws. That theorem's statement covers only two real random variables: 'Two real random variables have the same law exactly when their cumulative distribution functions agree' (handbook/parts/p15/measurable-probability.tex lines 443-444). The handbook also defines a cumulative distribution function only for a real random variable (lines 417-425). mu_F is never exhibited as the law of a real random variable, for example the identity map on (R, B(R), mu_F). The same holds for an arbitrary Borel probability measure with the same ray values. No direct argument is written either: neither the ray pi-system route (thm:p15-measure-uniqueness with thm:p15-borel-generators) nor the uniqueness clause of thm:p15-stieltjes-construction. So the equality-of-laws and uniqueness conclusions lack a written step.

defect_observations.observation: The endpoint-limit step writes out only the lower end. The upper end is given as 'The upper-end proof is the reversed argument'. The missing steps are short: when sup F is finite, choose a point whose value is within epsilon of it, and monotonicity bounds every point to its right; when sup F is infinite, choose points above any bound. They are still owed. The C009 and C012 proofs use this theorem's conclusions. Each of them is judged here on its own written steps.

The stated conclusion 'Its values on bounded intervals are finite' gets no derivation for closed, open or left-closed bounded intervals. One sentence would supply it: containment in some (-n,n] plus monotonicity.

The cited theorem's scope does not match how it is used. thm:p15-cdf-laws is stated for real random variables, but here it is applied to mu_F and to all Borel probability laws with cumulative function F. One bridging sentence would close the gap. Either realize a Borel probability measure as the law of the identity map, or apply thm:p15-measure-uniqueness directly to the ray pi-system.

This is a source variant observation, not counted as a failure. Durrett's semialgebra definition (held source, printed p. 3, PDF 11) requires only closure under intersection and the complement property. The handbook also requires the empty set to belong to S, without saying that this differs from the source. No result in scope depends on the difference, since S_R contains the empty set in both texts. The scope record that lists the 'identified source variants' is under spec/research and was excluded from this audit, so the variants checked were limited to those visible in the held source. Each visible variant was found preserved: 'measure on an algebra' (p. 4); existence of the extension without sigma-finiteness (pp. 458-459), as against the sigma-finite statement of Thm 1.1.9 and A.1.3; the inverse sup{y: F(y) < omega} on (0,1) with Lebesgue measure (Thm 1.2.2, p. 11); and Stieltjes endpoint values with F(infinity) > -infinity and F(-infinity) < infinity (p. 5).
